questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties
questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (2F-G)$ at the point $(0,-1,2)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)={e}^{x}\,i+yz\,j,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=z\,i+(x+2y)\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F-G) & =∇\times (2F)+∇\times (-G) \\  & =2∇\times F-∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ {e}^{x} & yz & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(0)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(yz)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(0)-\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{x})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(yz)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x})]k \\  & =(0-y)i-(0-0)j+(0-0)k \\  & =-y\,i.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F-G) & =2∇\times F-∇\times G \\  & =2[-y\,i]-[z\,i+(x+2y)\,k] \\  & =-2y\,i-z\,i-(x+2y)\,k \\  & =-(2y+z)\,i-(x+2y)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,-1,2),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (2F-G))(0,-1,2) & =-(2(-1)+2)\,i-(0+2(-1))\,k \\  & =-(-2+2)\,i-(0-2)\,k \\  & =2\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F+G)$ at the point $(0,1,2)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)={x}^{2}z\,i+xz\,j-\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,i-{z}^{2}\,j-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+G) & =∇\times F+∇\times G\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ {x}^{2}z & xz & -\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xz)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}z)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xz)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}z)]k \\  & =(-\operatorname{cos}⁡y-x)i-(0-{x}^{2})j+(z-0)k \\  & =(-\operatorname{cos}⁡y-x)\,i+{x}^{2}\,j+z\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+G) & =∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =(-\operatorname{cos}⁡y-x)\,i+{x}^{2}\,j+z\,k+\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,i-{z}^{2}\,j-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,k \\  & =-x\,i+({x}^{2}-{z}^{2})\,j+(z-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,1,2),$ we get

$$
(∇\times (F+G))(0,1,2)=-4\,j+2\,k.
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F+3G)$ at the point $(0,1,-2)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)={y}^{2}\,i+z\,j+{x}^{2}\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=-3{x}^{2}\,j-k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+3G) & =∇\times F+∇\times (3G) \\  & =∇\times F+3∇\times G\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ {y}^{2} & z & {x}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}({y}^{2})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})]k \\  & =(0-1)i-(2x-0)j+(0-2y)k \\  & =-i-2x\,j-2y\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+3G) & =∇\times F+3∇\times G \\  & =-i-2x\,j-2y\,k+3[-3{x}^{2}\,j-k] \\  & =-i-2x\,j-2y\,k-9{x}^{2}\,j-3k \\  & =-i-(9{x}^{2}+2x)\,j-(2y+3)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,1,-2),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F+3G))(0,1,-2) & =-i-(9(0)^{2}+2(0))\,j-(2(1)+3)\,k \\  & =-i-5\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (2F+G)$ at the point $(-1,2,0)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=xyz\,i+xy\,j+{z}^{2}\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=xy\,j-x\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F+G) & =∇\times (2F)+∇\times G \\  & =2∇\times F+∇\times G\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ xyz & xy & {z}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xyz)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz)]k \\  & =(0-0)i-(0-xy)j+(y-xz)k \\  & =xy\,j+(y-xz)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F+G) & =2∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =2[xy\,j+(y-xz)\,k]+xy\,j-x\,k \\  & =2xy\,j+2(y-xz)\,k+xy\,j-x\,k \\  & =3xy\,j+(2y-2xz-x)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(-1,2,0),$ we get

$$
(∇\times (2F+G))(-1,2,0)=-6\,j+5\,k.
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F-2G)$ at the point $(2,\frac{\pi }{2},-1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=xy\,i+xz\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,i-x\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-2G) & =∇\times F-∇\times (2G) \\  & =∇\times F-2∇\times G\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ xy & xz & \operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{cos}⁡y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xz)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xz)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)]k \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡y-x)i-(0-0)j+(z-x)k \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡y-x)\,i+(z-x)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-2G) & =∇\times F-2∇\times G \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡y-x)\,i+(z-x)\,k-2[-\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,i-x\,k] \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡y-x)\,i+(z-x)\,k+2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,i+2x\,k \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡y-x)\,i+(z+x)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(2,\frac{\pi }{2},-1),$ we get

$$
(∇\times (F-2G))(2,\frac{\pi }{2},-1)=-\,i+k.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x,0,yz⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=y-{x}^{2}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨z,0,0⟩,\,∇f=⟨-2x,1,0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(0,2,-1).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2x & 1 & 0 \\ x & 0 & yz\end{aligned}| \\  & =[1(yz)-0(0)]i-[-2x(yz)-0(x)]j+[-2x(0)-1(x)]k \\  & =yz\,i+2xyz\,j-x\,k \\  & =⟨yz,2xyz,-x⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(y-{x}^{2})⟨z,0,0⟩+⟨yz,2xyz,-x⟩ \\  & =⟨z(y-{x}^{2}),0,0⟩+⟨yz,2xyz,-x⟩ \\  & =⟨z(2y-{x}^{2}),2xyz,-x⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(0,2,-1) & =⟨(-1)(2(2)-(0)^{2}),2(0)(2)(-1),-0⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡z,y,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=xyz.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩,\,∇f=⟨yz,xz,xy⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,1,0).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ yz & xz & xy \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡z & y & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[(xz)(0)-(y)(xy)]i-[(yz)(0)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xy)]j+[(yz)(y)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)(xz)]k \\  & =-x{y}^{2}\,i+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,j+(z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z)\,k \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =xyz⟨0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z,0⟩+⟨-x{y}^{2},xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xyz\operatorname{sin}⁡z+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z,z{y}^{2}-xz\operatorname{cos}⁡z⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{y}^{2},-xy(z\operatorname{sin}⁡z-\operatorname{cos}⁡z),z({y}^{2}-x\operatorname{cos}⁡z)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,0) & =⟨-1,-(0\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0),0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨0,x,2\sqrt{y}⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=y{z}^{2}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}},0,1⟩,\,∇f=⟨0,{z}^{2},2yz⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(0,4,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & {z}^{2} & 2yz \\ 0 & x & 2\sqrt{y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[({z}^{2})(2\sqrt{y})-(x)(2yz)]i-[(0)(2\sqrt{y})-(0)(2yz)]j+[(0)(x)-(0)({z}^{2})]k \\  & =(2{z}^{2}\sqrt{y}-2xyz)\,i+0\,j+0\,k \\  & =⟨2{z}^{2}\sqrt{y}-2xyz,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(y{z}^{2})⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}},0,1⟩+⟨2{z}^{2}\sqrt{y}-2xyz,0,0⟩ \\  & =⟨{z}^{2}\sqrt{y},0,y{z}^{2}⟩+⟨2{z}^{2}\sqrt{y}-2xyz,0,0⟩ \\  & =⟨3{z}^{2}\sqrt{y}-2xyz,0,y{z}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
∇\times (f\,F)(0,4,1)=⟨6,0,4⟩.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨y\operatorname{ln}⁡x,0,z⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=\frac{x}{y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩,\,∇f=⟨\frac{1}{y},-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,1,3).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}} & 0 \\ y\operatorname{ln}⁡x & 0 & z\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}(z)-0(0)]i-[\frac{1}{y}(z)-0(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]j+[\frac{1}{y}(0)-(-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}})(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]k \\  & =-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}}\,i-\frac{z}{y}\,j+\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}\,k \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =\frac{x}{y}⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,-\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,3) & =⟨-\frac{1(3)}{(1)^{2}},-\frac{3}{1},0⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-3,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+z),y,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=1+{z}^{2}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z),0⟩,\,∇f=⟨0,0,2z⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(\pi ,1,0).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 0 & 2z \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(x+z) & y & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[0(0)-2z(y)]i-[0(0)-2z\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+z)]j+[0(y)-0\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+z)]k \\  & =-2yz\,i+2z\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+z)j+0\,k \\  & =⟨-2yz,2z\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+z),0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(1+{z}^{2})⟨0,\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z),0⟩+⟨-2yz,2z\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+z),0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,(1+{z}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z),0⟩+⟨-2yz,2z\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+z),0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2yz,(1+{z}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z)+2z\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+z),0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(\pi ,1,0) & =⟨-2(1)(0),(1+(0)^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi +0)+2(0)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi +0),0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties
canonical_examples.problem:
Calculate $\nabla\times(3\mathbf{F} + \mathbf{G})$ at the point $(-1,1,0)$ for the vector fields $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G,$ where

$$
\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = 3x\,\mathbf{i} + y^2z\,\mathbf{j} + 2\,\mathbf{k}, \quad (\nabla\times\mathbf{G})(x,y,z) = 3y^2\,\mathbf{i} + 4z\,\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}.
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
If $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $\nabla \times (k \mathbf F) = k \nabla \times \mathbf F$

- $\nabla \times (\mathbf F + \mathbf G) = \nabla \times \mathbf F + \nabla \times \mathbf G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (3F+G) & =∇\times (3F)+∇\times G \\  & =3∇\times F+∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $\nabla \times \mathbf{F}.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ 3x & {y}^{2}z & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(2)-\frac{∂}{∂z}({y}^{2}z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(2)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(3x)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(3x)]k \\  & =(0-{y}^{2})i-(0-0)j+(0-0)k \\  & =-{y}^{2}\,i.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (3F+G) & =3∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =3[-{y}^{2}\,i]+[3{y}^{2}\,i+4z\,j+k] \\  & =-3{y}^{2}\,i+3{y}^{2}\,i+4z\,j+k \\  & =(3{y}^{2}-3{y}^{2})\,i+4z\,j+k \\  & =4z\,j+k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(-1,1,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-G))(-1,1,0) & =4(0)\,j+k=k.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z) =  \langle 0, y-z, x-y\rangle$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z) = x+y.$ Given that

$$
\nabla\times \mathbf F = \langle 0,\,-1,\,0\rangle, 
\quad
\nabla f = \langle 1,\, 1,\, 0\rangle,
$$

calculate $\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F)$ at the point $(-1,1,3).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+   \nabla f \times \mathbf F
$$

First, we compute $\nabla f \times \mathbf F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & y-z & x-y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[1\cdot (x-y)-0\cdot (y-z)]\,i-[1\cdot (x-y)-0\cdot (0)]\,j+[1\cdot (y-z)-1\cdot (0)]\,k \\  & =(x-y)\,i+(y-x)\,j+(y-z)\,k \\  & =⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x+y)⟨0,-1,0⟩+⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-(x+y),0⟩+⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩ \\  & =⟨x-y,\,-2x,\,y-z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(-1,1,3) & =⟨(-1)-1,\,-2(-1),\,1-3⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
